| `x-tsurara-type` / type mappings | The `go` entry, or `go.typeMappings` and `go.overrides`: a type with the import path of its package (`{ type: uuid.UUID, import: { from: github.com/google/uuid } }`, `{ type: time.Time, import: { from: time } }`) |

### Approximations

| Construct | Approximation |
|---|---|
| Untagged unions | The first member that decodes wins; struct members are decoded with unknown fields disallowed, so that an object does not match every struct. Required fields are not checked |
| Required properties | Not checked when decoding: a missing one is the zero value |
| Nullable required properties | A missing value decodes as `nil` |
| `const` | Its scalar type |
| Tuples | `[]any` |
| String and number constraints, `oneOf` exclusivity | Not checked |
| Integers written with a fraction (`1.0`) | Rejected by `encoding/json` |
| Properties whose names a struct tag cannot hold (with `"`, `\\`, `,`, `'` or a backquote, or empty) | Left out, with a warning |
| Tagged unions | `Unknown` is added where values are received; enums need no fallback, since a named type keeps any value |

## Layout and naming

One package in the output directory (Go cannot split a package across directories without import cycles). One file per declaration (`pet_gen.go`) and per operation (`get_pet_by_id_op_gen.go`), and `tsurara_gen.go` with the package documentation and the runtime version. File names end in `_gen.go`, so that no name ends in a build constraint (`_linux.go`, `_test.go`). Every file starts with `// Code generated by tsurara. DO NOT EDIT.`, the line Go tools recognize, and is printed as `gofmt` would (aligned fields, tags and comments), since backends run no formatter (18.8). Descriptions become `//` comments without their indentation and blank lines, so that gofmt finds no code blocks, lists or headings to rewrite.

Everything is exported: types, fields, constants and functions are PascalCase with Go's initialisms (`ID`, `URL`, `HTTP`, `JSON`, `API`, ... as golint lists them, also in the plural: `PetID`, `PhotoURLs`, `GetPetByID`). A name whose first letter has no upper case gets `X` (`X日本語`), one that starts with a digit `V`. Enum constants are the type's name and the value (`PetStatusAvailable`), or the member name of `x-enum-varnames` or `x-enumNames` when the definition gives one (`PetStatusInStock`). All of them share the package scope. Functions keep their operation's name: a schema with the same name moves aside, as `{Name}Body` when it is that operation's request body (`toggleAll` with the schema `ToggleAll` gives `ToggleAll(ctx, c, body ToggleAllBody, nil)`), otherwise as `{Name}Model`. Other collisions are numbered in claim order (types, constants, then functions). Go's keywords and predeclared identifiers are lower case, so exported names never collide with them; only names that would be empty or start with a digit change (`V1`). Fields are named per struct, after the names the struct uses itself (`AdditionalProperties`), and carry their JSON key in the tag.

## Call functions and results

```go
func GetPetByID(ctx context.Context, c *tsurara.Client, petID int64, opts *GetPetByIDOptions) (*tsurara.Success[Pet], error)
```

- The doc comment starts with the function's name (`// GetPetByID calls GET /pet/{petId}.`), followed by the summary and description.
- The context cancels the call and carries deadlines. Required parameters and a required body are arguments; everything optional is a pointer field of `{Operation}Options`, and `opts` may be `nil`.
- A body with several media types is a wrapper struct `{Operation}Body` with one pointer per media type (`JSON *Pet`, `Form *Pet`, `OctetStream *tsurara.File`); the field that is set picks the `Content-Type`.
- `*tsurara.Success[T]` has `Status`, `Data T`, `Headers` and `Operation`. `T` is the success body type: a response without content is `struct{}` (or the zero value of the other response's type), different types `any`; a response with a JSON media type is read as JSON (as in Rust). Binary responses are `[]byte`, text responses `string` with the bytes as they arrive (the standard library has no charsets but UTF-8; convert another `charset` with `golang.org/x/text`).
- Server-Sent Events, JSON Lines and JSON text sequences with an item schema (`itemSchema`, or `x-itemSchema` before 3.2; design.md 8.5) are `*tsurara.Success[*tsurara.Items[T]]` when every success is read item by item: the function calls `tsurara.DoItems` and returns once the headers have arrived, and `for item, err := range s.Data.All()` reads them. Events are a union wrapper with one pointer per event (`StreamEvent{StreamNoteEvent *StreamNoteEvent; ...; Unknown json.RawMessage}`), selected by `event`; several names of one event are a named type with constants (`MixedPingEventNamePong`). Leaving the loop closes the response, `Close` closes it without reading, and the client's timeout does not cover reading the items (the context does). With a JSON media type next to the stream, the operation is read as JSON as above.
- The error is `*tsurara.Failure[E]` for every outcome of the contract except success, with `Kind` (`tsurara.KindHTTP`, `KindNetwork`, `KindTimeout`, `KindParse`, `KindUnexpected`, `KindAborted`), `Status`, `Documented` with the documented error body `E` when there is one, the raw body otherwise, and `Cause`. It unwraps to the cause, so `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` works. `errors.As(err, &failure)` with `var failure *tsurara.Failure[Problem]` gives the operation's documented body; `var f tsurara.AnyFailure` reads the failure of any operation, with `f.Info()` (`Kind`, `Status`, `Documented`, `Headers`, `Cause`, `Operation`).
- OperationDefs are the JSON of `spec/operation-def.schema.json`, embedded as a string and parsed once (`sync.OnceValue`).
- `tsurara_gen.go` records the runtime version the code needs (`// Requires github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/runtimes/go v0.1.0`); `tsurara check` compares it with the requirement in the nearest `go.mod` (the same minor version), and only reports a module that a `replace` directive points elsewhere.
- Arguments are lower camel case (`petID`); names that Go reserves or the function uses (`type`, `string`, `ctx`, `opts`) are numbered (`type2`). Options fields are exported like struct fields.

## Options

```yaml
language: go
go:
  package: petstore                              # default: the output directory's name
  runtimeModule: github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/runtimes/go
  typeMappings:                                  # per format
    date-time: { type: time.Time, import: { from: time } }
  overrides:                                     # per JSON Pointer
    "#/components/schemas/Id": int64
```

## Types without the client

With `operations: false` the package has only the declarations: no operation files, nothing that imports `net/http` or `context`. The runtime stays one package; generated types use only its union helpers (`types.go`, `value.go`), and the linker leaves out the client when nothing calls it. The types are plain `encoding/json` types:

```go
var pet petstore.Pet
err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(`{"id":1,"name":"Pochi"}`), &pet)
```

## Mocks

With `go.mocks: true`, `mocks_gen.go` is in the generated package with the build tag `tsurara_mocks`, so production builds leave it out and tests run with `go test -tags tsurara_mocks`:

- `Mock{Type}()` decodes the sample value of each declaration.
- Per operation, a constructor per documented status (`ShowPetByIDMock200(body Pet)`, `ShowPetByIDMockDefault(status int, body Error)`) and `ShowPetByIDRoute(respond)` for `tsuraratest` (nil: the first documented success); `MockRoutes()` lists every operation.

Its names are claimed after every other name of the package, so turning mocks on never renames generated code.

## Using it

Generate into a directory of your module (`output: internal/petstore`), require the runtime (`go get github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/runtimes/go`), and call the functions:

```go
c := tsurara.NewClient("https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3")
pets, err := petstore.FindPetsByStatus(ctx, c, petstore.FindPetsByStatusStatusAvailable, nil)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
for _, pet := range pets.Data {
	fmt.Println(pet.Name)
}
```

<!-- docs/languages/python.md -->

# Python

The Python backend (`language: python`, crate `tsurara-lang-python`) generates dataclasses, enums and type aliases, with TypeDefs for a runtime that converts JSON generically (design.md 18.7). Generated code uses the runtime `tsurara-client` (`runtimes/python`): sync and async clients over httpx, Results, and the TypeDef codec; it passes the conformance vectors in `spec/`. Each operation gets a call function.

Generated code requires Python 3.11 or later (design.md 18.15, Q2) and is checked with pyright as Python 3.11.

## Quick start

Install the generator (`npm install --save-dev tsurara`, or a binary from the [GitHub releases](https://github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/releases)), then write `tsurara.config.yaml`:

```yaml
input: https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3/openapi.json
output: api
language: python
```

```sh
tsurara generate
pip install "tsurara-client[http]"     # the runtime, with httpx
```

```python
from tsurara_client import Client, Success, unwrap
from api import PetStatus
from api.operations import find_pets_by_status, get_pet_by_id

with Client("https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3") as client:
    pets = unwrap(find_pets_by_status(client, status=PetStatus.AVAILABLE))
    match get_pet_by_id(client, pet_id=1):
        case Success(data=pet):
            print(pet.name)
```

## Capabilities

`tsurara_lang_python::CAPABILITIES` (design.md 18.5.2):

| Capability | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `inline_records` | no | Inline objects become dataclasses named after their place (`PetOwner`) |
| `structural_unions` | yes | `A \| B` |
| `tagged_unions` | yes | Written as a union alias; the tag is in the TypeDef |
| `intersections` | no | `allOf` becomes a dataclass: a base class for one reference, copied fields otherwise |
| `inheritance` | single | Dataclass inheritance |
| `literal_types` | yes | `Literal["cat"]` |
| `enums` | any | `Enum` classes |
| `tuples` | yes | One `tuple[...]` per allowed length |
| `strict_decoding` | yes | Enums and discriminators are open where values are received, unless `strictEnums` |
| `nullable_primitives` | yes | `X \| None` |
| `recursion_by_value` | yes | |

## Mapping

| Model | Python |
|---|---|
| Object | `@dataclass(kw_only=True)` class; `kw_only` lets required fields follow defaulted ones, also through inheritance |
| Required property | `name: T` |
| Optional property | `name: T \| None = None` |
| Nullable property | `name: T \| None` |
| Optional and nullable | `name: T \| None \| Missing = MISSING` (`_support.py`); missing and `null` differ only here (Q3) |
| `additionalProperties` | `additional_properties: dict[str, T] = field(default_factory=dict)` |
| Enum | `class Status(Enum)` with members named from the values (`IT_S`, `VALUE_1`), or from `x-enum-varnames` or `x-enumNames` when the definition has them; at a received site the annotation is `Status \| str` (or `\| int`) |
| Open tagged union | At a received site, `Cat \| Dog \| dict[str, Any]`: an unlisted discriminator keeps the JSON object |
| Object with only `additionalProperties` | `dict[str, T]` |
| `oneOf`, `anyOf`, type arrays | `Name: TypeAlias = "A \| B"` |
| `integer`, `number`, `string`, `boolean` | `int`, `float`, `str`, `bool`; `format` is kept in the TypeDefs (dates stay `str` until the runtime converts them) |
| Array, map | `list[T]`, `dict[str, T]` |
| `prefixItems` | `tuple[A] \| tuple[A, B] \| tuple[A, B, *tuple[R, ...]]` |
| Binary | `bytes \| File` (`File` from the runtime adds a file name and a media type); binary responses are `bytes` |
| `x-tsurara-type` / type mappings | The `python` entry; without one, the schema's type and an `unmapped-type` warning |

### Approximations

| Construct | Approximation |
|---|---|
| `allOf` with a member that is not an object | One member is kept, with a warning (design.md 18.5.3, pass 2) |
| `allOf` with several references | Fields are copied; the dataclass does not inherit from them |
| String and number constraints, `oneOf` exclusivity | Not checked by the types, as in TypeScript |
| Discriminated unions | The union alias accepts any member; the TypeDef selects by the tag |

## Layout and naming

One module per declaration (`pet.py`, `pet_owner.py`), `__init__.py` re-exporting every class, `_typedefs.py` with `TYPE_DEFS` and `CODEC` (the TypeDefs with this package's classes), and `_support.py`. Modules start with `from __future__ import annotations` and import the classes their annotations use under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`; only a base class is imported at run time, so recursive and mutually referencing types never form import cycles. Type aliases are strings for the same reason.

Classes are PascalCase (component names that are identifiers are kept), members snake_case per class, with keywords and soft keywords getting `_` (`class_`, `type_`); a member whose JSON key differs gets a `# JSON: "..."` comment, and the TypeDef records the key. Names that generated modules use themselves (`Any`, `Enum`, `File`, `Missing`, ...) get `Model`. Modules are snake_case and case-folded.

## Call functions

`operations/` has one module per operation, named after its function (`operations/get_pet_by_id.py`), and `operations/__init__.py` re-exports the functions and their Result types. Each module has the OperationDef as `DEF` (with TypeDef references for the runtime), the Result type, and the function:

```python
from api import PetStatus
from api.operations import get_pet_by_id, find_pets_by_status
from tsurara_client import Client, Success, unwrap

with Client("https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3") as client:
    match get_pet_by_id(client, pet_id=1):
        case Success(data=pet):
            print(pet.name)
    pets = unwrap(find_pets_by_status(client, status=PetStatus.AVAILABLE))
```

- Parameters are keyword-only, snake_case, after `client`. Optional parameters default to `None`, which means not sent. A parameter named like an argument the function has itself (`body`, `timeout`, ...) gets a number (`body2`), and keywords get `_` (`class_`).
- `body` is the request body (`None` by default when optional); with several media types, `content_type` picks one (`Literal[...]`), the first by default.
- `timeout` (seconds) and `context` (passed to hooks) are per call.
- With `AsyncClient` the same function returns an awaitable (`@overload`).
- The Result type is `Success[...] | HttpError[...] | UndocumentedStatus | TransportFailure`: the success data per documented status and media type (`None` without content), and the documented error bodies. `default` is an error when other successes are documented.
- Server-Sent Events, JSON Lines and JSON text sequences with an item schema (`itemSchema`, or `x-itemSchema` before 3.2; design.md 8.5) are read item by item: the success data is `Iterator[StreamEvent]` with `Client` and `AsyncIterator[StreamEvent]` with `AsyncClient`, so such an operation has a second Result type, `{Operation}AsyncResult`. Events are dataclasses of a union tagged by `event` (`StreamNoteEvent`, with `data` decoded as its `contentSchema`); events the definition does not list arrive as dicts. Items of JSON Lines are their item schema's type (`{Operation}Item` when it is inline).
- Generated code needs `tsurara-client>=0.1,<0.2`; `operations/__init__.py` says so. `tsurara check` does not check the installed Python runtime yet.

## Types without the client

With `operations: false` there is no `operations` package, and the output needs `tsurara-client` without the `http` extra: `import tsurara_client` and the TypeDef codec use only the standard library. Decode JSON with the generated codec:

```python
from api import Pet
from api._typedefs import CODEC

pet = CODEC.decode({"ref": "Pet"}, {"id": 1, "name": "Pochi"})
assert isinstance(pet, Pet)
CODEC.encode({"ref": "Pet"}, pet)  # {"id": 1, "name": "Pochi"}
```

Call functions import the client, which needs httpx: install `tsurara-client[http]` (the generated `operations/__init__.py` names it). Importing `Client` without httpx raises an `ImportError` that says so.

## Mocks

With `python.mocks: true`, the subpackage `mocks` has the values of the TypeScript mocks (design.md 8.9), built from the same samples (18.7.1):

- `mocks/schemas.py`: `mock_pet(**overrides) -> Pet` decodes the sample with the package's TypeDefs; dataclasses take field overrides (`dataclasses.replace`).
- `mocks/operations.py`: per operation, a constructor per documented status (`show_pet_by_id_200(body: Pet)`, `show_pet_by_id_default(status, body)`) and `show_pet_by_id_route(response=None)`, a route for `MockRouter` that answers with the first documented success by default; `routes()` lists every operation.

```python
router = MockRouter(base_path="/v1")
router.extend(routes())
client = Client("https://api.test/v1", http=httpx.Client(transport=httpx.MockTransport(router)))
```

## Options

```yaml
language: python
python:
  strictEnums: false   # true: unlisted enum and discriminator values are errors where received
```

<!-- docs/languages/rust.md -->

# Rust

The Rust backend (`language: rust`, crate `tsurara-lang-rust`) generates structs and enums with serde derives, and async call functions for the runtime crate `tsurara-client` (`runtimes/rust`). This document describes the mapping. The backend is experimental: `tsurara generate` says so, and its output may change.

Generated code compiles with Rust 1.85 (the generator's MSRV) and depends only on `tsurara-client`, which re-exports `serde` and `serde_json`: derives name the crate with `#[serde(crate = "tsurara_client::serde")]`, so users add one dependency.

## Capabilities

`tsurara_lang_rust::CAPABILITIES` (design.md 18.5.2):

| Capability | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `inline_records` | no | Inline objects become structs named after their place (`PetOwner`) |
| `structural_unions` | no | Unions become enums |
| `tagged_unions` | yes | Enums selected by the discriminator |
| `intersections` | no | `allOf` becomes one struct with the fields copied (Rust has no inheritance) |
| `inheritance` | none | |
| `literal_types` | no | A `const` is its scalar type |
| `enums` | any | String enums are Rust enums; integer and mixed enums become constants of their scalar type |
| `tuples` | yes | Fixed-length tuples `(A, B)`; other tuples `Vec<serde_json::Value>` |
| `strict_decoding` | yes | serde fails on unlisted values, so received enums and discriminators are open |
| `nullable_primitives` | yes | `Option<T>` |
| `recursion_by_value` | no | `Box<T>` on fields that close a cycle (pass 10), also cycles through unions |

## Value conversion

Annotations (design.md 18.7): serde derives and attributes. Constructs serde's derives cannot express go through macros of `tsurara-client`, which generated code invokes but does not implement. OperationDefs carry no TypeDef references.

## Mapping

| Model | Rust |
|---|---|
| Object | `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct Pet { ... }` |
| Required property | `pub name: T`, with `#[serde(rename = "...")]` when the JSON key differs from the field name |
| Optional property | `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub name: Option<T>` |
| Nullable property | `pub name: Option<T>` (`null` is `None`; a missing value is accepted too, a wider type) |
| Optional and nullable | `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Nullable::is_missing")] pub name: tsurara_client::Nullable<T>`, an enum of `Missing`, `Null` and `Value(T)` (Q3) |
| `additionalProperties` | `#[serde(flatten)] pub additional_properties: BTreeMap<String, T>` |
| String enum | `pub enum Status { #[serde(rename = "available")] Available, ... }`, variants named from `x-enum-varnames` or `x-enumNames` when the definition has them; where values are received, also `#[serde(untagged)] Unknown(String)`, which keeps an unlisted value and writes it back |
| Integer or mixed enum | `pub type Level = i64;` with `pub const LEVEL_1: Level = 1;` |
| Discriminated union | `pub enum Pet { Cat(Cat), Dog(Dog) }` with `tsurara_client::tagged_union!`, which reads the discriminator and decodes the member from the whole object (the member keeps its tag field); the `defaultMapping` member takes unlisted values, and otherwise, where received, `Unknown(serde_json::Value)` does |
| Other unions (`oneOf`, `anyOf`, type arrays) | `#[serde(untagged)] pub enum Id { Integer(i64), String(String) }`, members tried in order; variant names from the member types |
| `allOf` | One struct with the fields of every member |
| Alias | `pub type Name = T;`; an alias that contains itself (`Tree: { type: array, items: { $ref: Tree } }`) is a newtype, `#[serde(transparent)] pub struct Tree(pub Vec<Tree>);` |
| `$ref` cycles | `Box<T>` on the fields that close the cycle |
| `integer` (`int32`, `int64`, none) | `i32`, `i64`, `i64` |
| `number` | `f64` |
| `string` (any format), `boolean` | `String`, `bool`; formats are in the docs, and type mappings can name other types |
| Array, map | `Vec<T>`, `BTreeMap<String, T>` |
| `{}`, external without a `rust` entry | `serde_json::Value` |
| Binary | `tsurara_client::File` where sent (bodies, multipart parts); `Vec<u8>` for responses |
| `x-tsurara-type` / type mappings | The `rust` entry, a path with generics (`uuid::Uuid`, `chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>`) |

### Approximations

| Construct | Approximation |
|---|---|
| Nullable required properties | A missing value decodes as `None` |
| `const` | Its scalar type |
| Tuples with optional or rest elements | `Vec<serde_json::Value>` |
| Untagged unions | The first member that decodes wins, as in every TypeDef runtime |
| Discriminated unions with a member no value selects | An untagged union with the same members (an inline member selects by its property's `const` or `enum`; without one, nothing names it) |
| Integer enums | Not checked: any integer decodes |
| Integers written with a fraction (`1.0`) | Rejected, where the TypeDef runtimes coerce them |
| String and number constraints, `oneOf` exclusivity | Not checked |

## Layout and naming

The output directory is a module: `mod.rs` declares `pub mod types;` and `pub mod operations;`, `types/mod.rs` declares one module per declaration (`types/pet.rs`) and re-exports every type, and each type module starts with `use super::*;`. Users include it with `mod api;` (or `#[path = "..."]`). No `Cargo.toml` is generated (Q5).

Types are PascalCase, fields, functions and modules snake_case, enum variants and constants as their case requires. Keywords become raw identifiers for fields and functions (`r#type`), and get `Model` as types; names the generated code uses (`Option`, `Result`, `String`, `Vec`, `Box`, `BTreeMap`, `Nullable`, `File`, `Value`) get `Model` too. A field whose JSON key differs gets `#[serde(rename = "...")]`.

## Call functions and results

One async function per operation in `operations/` (`operations/get_pet_by_id.rs`, re-exported from `operations`):

```rust
pub async fn get_pet_by_id(
    client: &tsurara_client::Client,
    pet_id: i64,                    // required parameters, in definition order
    options: GetPetByIdOptions,     // optional parameters, an optional body, and `timeout`
) -> tsurara_client::ApiResult<Pet, Problem>
```

- Required parameters and a required body are arguments. Everything optional is a field of the operation's `{Operation}Options`, which derives `Default` (`get_pet_by_id(&client, 1, Default::default())`). For an optional parameter that allows `null`, `None` leaves it out; `null` cannot be sent on its own.
- A body with several media types is an enum `{Operation}Body` with one variant per media type (`Json(Pet)`, `Form(Pet)`, `OctetStream(tsurara_client::File)`, `Multipart(...)`); the variant picks the `Content-Type`.
- Binary bodies and multipart file parts are `tsurara_client::File`: bytes with an optional file name and media type. A multipart body is a struct whose fields become parts in order; a list of files becomes one part per file.
- `ApiResult<S, E> = Result<Success<S>, Failure<E>>`. `S` is the success body type and `E` the documented error body type. A response without content is `()`. When the responses have one type and no content, it is `Option<T>`; when they have different types, `serde_json::Value`. Binary responses are `Vec<u8>`, text responses `String`.
- Server-Sent Events, JSON Lines and JSON text sequences with an item schema (`itemSchema`, or `x-itemSchema` before 3.2; design.md 8.5) are `tsurara_client::Items<T>` when every success is read item by item: the function calls `Client::request_items` and returns once the headers have arrived, and `items.next().await` gives each item as `Result<T, ItemError>`. Events are a union tagged by `event` (`StreamEvent::StreamNoteEvent(StreamNoteEvent)` and so on, and `Unknown` for names the definition does not list). Dropping `Items` closes the response, and the client's timeout does not cover reading the items. With a JSON media type next to the stream, the operation is read as JSON as below.
- A response with a JSON media type is read as JSON, and a body in its other media types is a `Parse` failure. tsurara sends no `Accept`, so servers answer with their default media type, which is JSON for every corpus definition.
- `Failure` has the contract's kinds (`Http` with a documented or undocumented body, `Network`, `Timeout`, `Parse`, `Unexpected`) and implements `std::error::Error`, so `?` works. Dropping the future cancels the call; there is no `aborted` result, as in Python.
- OperationDefs are the JSON of `spec/operation-def.schema.json`, embedded as a raw string and parsed once (`LazyLock`).
- `mod.rs` records the runtime version the code needs (`// Requires tsurara-client ^0.1.0`); `tsurara check` compares it with `tsurara-client` in the nearest `Cargo.lock`.

### Using it

Generate into a directory of your crate (`output: src/api`), add the runtime (`cargo add tsurara-client`) and `mod api;`:

```rust
use api::operations::*;
use api::types::*;
use tsurara_client::{Client, Failure};

let client = Client::builder("https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3").build();
let pets = find_pets_by_status(&client, FindPetsByStatusStatus::Available, Default::default()).await?;
match get_pet_by_id(&client, 1, Default::default()).await {
    Ok(pet) => println!("{}", pet.data.name),
    Err(Failure::Http { status: 404, .. }) => println!("no such pet"),
    Err(other) => return Err(other.into()),
}
```

## Options

```yaml
language: rust
rust:
  runtimeCrate: tsurara_client   # the path generated code uses for the runtime
  typeMappings:               # per format
    date-time: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>
  overrides:                  # per JSON Pointer
    "#/components/schemas/Id": uuid::Uuid
```

## Types without the client

With `operations: false`, `mod.rs` declares only `types` (and `mocks` with `rust.mocks`), and the types need the runtime without its `client` feature:

```toml
[dependencies]
tsurara-client = { version = "0.1", default-features = false }
```

That leaves `Nullable`, `File`, `tagged_union!` and the re-exported `serde` and `serde_json`: no tokio, no reqwest. The types are plain serde types:

```rust
let pet: api::types::Pet = tsurara_client::serde_json::from_str(r#"{"id":1,"name":"Pochi"}"#)?;
```

The runtime's features: `client` (the client, Results, retries, sequences; tokio), `reqwest` (the default transport, enables `client`), `testing` (the mock transport). The default is `client` and `reqwest`.

## Mocks

With `rust.mocks: true`, the module `mocks` is declared under `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "mocks"))]`, so it is compiled for the crate's own tests and with a crate feature `mocks` that enables `tsurara-client/testing`:

- `mocks/schemas.rs`: `mock_pet() -> Pet` decodes the sample value; change fields with struct update syntax (`Pet { name: "Tama".into(), ..mock_pet() }`).
- `mocks/operations.rs`: per operation, `ShowPetByIdMockResponse` with a variant per documented status (`Status200(Pet)`, `Default(u16, Error)`) and `show_pet_by_id(mock, respond)`, which adds the route to a `MockTransport`; `routes(mock)` adds every operation with its first documented success.

## Compile time

Every type derives `Serialize`, `Deserialize`, `Debug`, `Clone` and `PartialEq`, and lives in its own module. On an Apple Silicon laptop (2026-11-17), `cargo clippy` of the output with call functions takes about 40 seconds for OpenAI (6,200 types), 110 seconds for GitHub 3.1 (8,200 types, 1,270 operations) and 100 seconds for Stripe (11,400 types); `cargo check` of OpenAI's types alone takes 14 seconds.

Each type module imports the types it uses by name (`use super::{Owner, Tag};`). Earlier versions imported their parent with a glob (`use super::*`), whose `pub use` globs cover every type module: name resolution became quadratic, and took 80 of OpenAI's 95 seconds of `cargo check` (`-Z time-passes`: `resolve_crate` 52 s, `compute_effective_visibilities` 29 s) while derive expansion took 23. Stripe did not finish in 90 minutes. What remains is spent in type checking, borrow checking and derive expansion, in about equal parts.

Generated code is a module of the user's crate; putting it in a crate of its own keeps it out of incremental rebuilds. Splitting the output by tag into features, and deriving only the direction a type is used in, would save little after the fix, and are not done.

name: tsurara
description: Write application code against API clients generated by tsurara from OpenAPI (TypeScript, Python, Rust, Go). Use when a project has `tsurara.config.yaml` or files starting with "Generated by tsurara", when calling an endpoint of such an API, handling its Results, using it with TanStack Query, changing what is generated, or testing code that calls it with the generated mocks.
---

# tsurara

tsurara generates types and one call function per operation from an OpenAPI definition. The generated code calls a small runtime (`@tsurara/client`, `tsurara-client` for Python and Rust, `github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/runtimes/go`). `tsurara.config.yaml` lists the targets: input definition, output directory, language and options.

## Rules

1. Never edit generated files. They start with a marker (`// Generated by tsurara. Do not edit.`, `# Generated by tsurara. Do not edit.`, `// Code generated by tsurara. DO NOT EDIT.`). Change the definition or `tsurara.config.yaml`, then run `tsurara generate`.
2. Call the generated function for an endpoint; do not build URLs or `fetch` requests by hand. Find it with `tsurara inspect operations --search "<words>"` or the MCP tool `search_operations`, then `tsurara inspect operation <id>` (or `describe_operation`) for its parameters and a call example that compiles.
3. Use what else is generated for the operation instead of writing it: TanStack Query options, keys and filters, and mock handlers and factories for tests. `inspect operation` lists them under "also generated" (`helpers` in JSON).
4. Calls return a Result instead of throwing (except Rust and Go, which return `Result`/`error` as the language does). Check success before using the data; use `unwrap` where an exception is the right failure.
5. Run `tsurara check` before finishing. It fails when generated files are stale or edited, or the runtime version does not match.
6. `tsurara generate` prints warnings with a code and a JSON Pointer into the definition; `tsurara inspect warning <code>` explains each and how to fix it.

## Finding answers

| Question | Command (add `--format json` to parse it) | MCP tool |
|---|---|---|
| Which targets and languages? | read `tsurara.config.yaml` | `list_targets` |
| Which function calls `GET /pets/{id}`? | `tsurara inspect operations --search "get pet"` | `search_operations` |
| How do I call it? | `tsurara inspect operation getPetById --target <name>` | `describe_operation` |
| What does the type `Pet` look like? | `tsurara inspect schema Pet --target <name>` | `describe_schema` |
| What does warning `renamed` mean? | `tsurara inspect warning renamed` | `explain_warning` |

## References

Read the one for the language you are writing:

- [references/typescript.md](references/typescript.md): Results, `unwrap`, `ApiError`, middleware
- [references/tanstack-query.md](references/tanstack-query.md): TanStack Query options, keys, scopes, infinite queries, retries, and MSW handlers for tests
- [references/python.md](references/python.md): `match` on Results, `unwrap`, async clients
- [references/rust.md](references/rust.md): `Result<Success, Failure>` and its variants
- [references/go.md](references/go.md): `(*Success[T], error)` and `*Failure[E]`
- [references/configuration.md](references/configuration.md): targets, `extends`, type mappings, validators, query options, mocks, hooks and plugins

<!-- skills/tsurara/references/configuration.md -->

# Configuration

`tsurara.config.yaml` (or `.json`, `.toml`) at the project root; `docs/guide/configuration.md` in the tsurara repository (or the MCP resource `tsurara://docs/guide/configuration.md`) lists every key.

```yaml
input: ./openapi.yaml            # a file or a URL
targets:
  - name: web
    output: ./web/src/api
    typescript:
      importExtension: ts        # js (default), ts or none
      validators: zod            # also generate Zod schemas for validateResponses
      validatorConstraints: true # and check minLength, pattern, minimum, ... in them
      query: tanstack            # TanStack Query options, keys and filters (query/)
      mocks: msw                 # MSW handlers and mock factories (mocks/); or fetch
      infiniteQueries:           # pagination of reads, for infinite query options
        listPets: { param: query.cursor, next: /nextCursor }
  - name: worker
    output: ./worker/api
    language: python
naming:
  overrides:
    "#/components/schemas/Error": ApiError   # rename by JSON Pointer
typeMappings:
  - match: { type: string, format: uuid }
    typescript: { type: Uuid, import: { from: ./ids.ts, name: Uuid } }
hooks:
  afterWrite:
    - [biome, format, --write, "{output}"]
```

- `extends: ./base.yaml` merges another file; paths stay relative to the file they are written in.
- `${ENV}` in strings is replaced with environment variables (an unset one is an error).
- Hooks: `transformDocument`, `transformModel`, `extend` (add files next to the generated code, with the manifest of generated names; see `docs/guide/plugins.md`), `transformFiles`, `afterWrite`.
- `tsurara init --preset react-query` writes a configuration with query options, Zod schemas and MSW handlers for a React app, and prints the packages to install.
- Pagination can also be written on the operation in the definition: `x-tsurara-pagination: { param: query.cursor, next: /nextCursor }`.
- Python, Rust and Go generate mocks with `python.mocks`, `rust.mocks` and `go.mocks: true`.
- After changing the definition or the configuration, run `tsurara generate`, then `tsurara check` in CI.

<!-- skills/tsurara/references/go.md -->

# Go

Each operation is a function in the generated package: `ctx`, the client, required parameters, the body, then `*{Op}Options` (or `nil`). It returns `(*tsurara.Success[T], error)`; failures are `*tsurara.Failure[E]`.

```go
package api

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	tsurara "github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/runtimes/go"
)

// PetName returns the name of a pet, or "" when it cannot be read.
func PetName(ctx context.Context, c *tsurara.Client, petID string) string {
	res, err := ShowPetByID(ctx, c, petID, nil)
	var failure *tsurara.Failure[Error]
	switch {
	case err == nil:
		return res.Data.Name
	case errors.As(err, &failure) && failure.Kind == tsurara.KindHTTP && failure.Documented:
		fmt.Println(failure.Status, failure.Body.Message)
	default:
		fmt.Println(err)
	}
	return ""
}

// NewPetClient creates the client for the API.
func NewPetClient() *tsurara.Client {
	return tsurara.NewClient("https://petstore.example.com/v1")
}
```

- Optional fields are pointers; types without a Go equivalent (unions) are wrapper structs with methods.
- `tsurara.NewClient` takes options: `WithHeader`, `WithTimeout`, `WithRetry`, `WithAuth`.
- Tests: with `go.mocks: true`, `mocks_gen.go` (build tag `tsurara_mocks`, so run `go test -tags tsurara_mocks`) has `Mock{Type}()`, a constructor per documented status and `{Op}Route(respond)` for `tsuraratest` (`docs/languages/go.md`, "Mocks").

<!-- skills/tsurara/references/python.md -->

# Python

Each operation is a function in `operations/<name>.py` taking the client first and keyword arguments after it; it returns a Result object. The same function works with `Client` and, awaited, with `AsyncClient`.

```python
from tsurara_client import Client, HttpError, Success, unwrap

from .operations.show_pet_by_id import show_pet_by_id
from .pet import Pet


def pet_name(pet_id: str) -> str | None:
    with Client("https://petstore.example.com/v1") as client:
        match show_pet_by_id(client, pet_id=pet_id):
            case Success(data=pet):
                return pet.name
            case HttpError(status=status, error=error):
                print(status, error)
            case other:
                print("failed:", other.kind)
    return None


def load_pet(client: Client[None], pet_id: str) -> Pet:
    # Raises ApiError on any failure.
    return unwrap(show_pet_by_id(client, pet_id=pet_id))
```

- Records are dataclasses and enums are `Enum` classes; the runtime converts JSON with the TypeDefs in `_typedefs.py` (`CODEC.decode` / `CODEC.encode`).
- Optional parameters are keyword arguments that default to `None`; a value that may be absent or `null` uses `MISSING` for absent.
- Tests: with `python.mocks: true`, `mocks/schemas.py` has `mock_pet(**overrides)` and `mocks/operations.py` a constructor per documented status and `show_pet_by_id_route(response=None)` per operation, for the `MockRouter` of `tsurara_client.testing` (`docs/languages/python.md`, "Mocks"). Use them instead of hand-written fixtures.

<!-- skills/tsurara/references/rust.md -->

# Rust

Each operation is an `async fn` in the generated `operations` module: required parameters are arguments, optional ones fields of `{Op}Options` (which implements `Default`). It returns `Result<Success<T>, Failure<E>>`.

```rust
use super::operations::show_pet_by_id;
use tsurara_client::{ErrorBody, Failure};

pub async fn pet_name(client: &tsurara_client::Client, pet_id: &str) -> Option<String> {
    match show_pet_by_id(client, pet_id.to_owned(), Default::default()).await {
        Ok(success) => Some(success.data.name),
        Err(Failure::Http {
            status,
            body: ErrorBody::Documented(error),
            ..
        }) => {
            eprintln!("{status}: {}", error.message);
            None
        }
        Err(failure) => {
            eprintln!("{failure:?}");
            None
        }
    }
}

pub fn client() -> tsurara_client::Client {
    tsurara_client::Client::builder("https://petstore.example.com/v1").build()
}
```

- Types are in the generated `types` module; optional fields are `Option<T>`, nullable ones `Nullable<T>`.
- The runtime re-exports `serde` and `serde_json`; generated code needs no other dependency.
- Tests: with `rust.mocks: true`, `mocks::schemas::mock_pet()` and per operation a `{Op}MockResponse` with a variant per documented status and a function that adds the route to the runtime's `MockTransport` (the `testing` feature; `docs/languages/rust.md`, "Mocks").

<!-- skills/tsurara/references/tanstack-query.md -->

# TanStack Query and mocks (TypeScript)

With `typescript.query: tanstack`, every operation also has options for TanStack Query 5 in `query/{function}.ts`, and with `typescript.mocks: msw` an MSW handler in `mocks/operations/{function}.ts`. Use them instead of writing a `queryFn`, a query key or a request handler by hand: `tsurara inspect operation <id>` (or `describe_operation`) lists them under "also generated". `tsurara init --preset react-query` turns both on; `docs/guide/react.md` walks through a complete app.

```ts
import {
  QueryClient,
  skipToken,
  useMutation,
  useQuery,
  useQueryClient,
} from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { createClient, isHttpError, queryRetry, queryScopeFilter } from '@tsurara/client';
import { createPetsMutationOptions } from './query/createPets.js';
import { listPetsQueryFilter } from './query/listPets.js';
import {
  setShowPetByIdQueriesData,
  showPetByIdQueryKey,
  showPetByIdQueryOptions,
} from './query/showPetById.js';

// One client per session; `queryScope` keeps the cache of tenants (or APIs) apart.
const scope = { tenant: 'acme' };
const api = createClient({ baseUrl: 'https://petstore.example.com/v1', queryScope: scope });

// Retries like the retry() middleware (network failures, 408, 429, 5xx), never 404 or 422.
const queryClient = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: queryRetry() } } });

export function usePetName(petId: string | undefined): string | undefined {
  // `skipToken` while the input is not known; `select` decides the type of `data`.
  const pet = useQuery({
    ...showPetByIdQueryOptions(api, petId === undefined ? skipToken : { path: { petId } }),
    select: (p) => p.name,
  });
  if (pet.error && pet.error.kind === 'http' && pet.error.status === 404) return undefined;
  return pet.data;
}

function useCreatePet() {
  const qc = useQueryClient();
  return useMutation({
    ...createPetsMutationOptions(api),
    onSuccess: async () => {
      // Every listPets query of this tenant, by the generated filter: no hand-written key.
      await qc.invalidateQueries(listPetsQueryFilter(scope));
    },
    onError: (error) => {
      // The documented error body, typed, when the status is documented.
      if (isHttpError(error.result, 500)) console.error(error.result.error.message);
    },
  });
}

export function renamePet(petId: string, name: string): void {
  // One entry by its key, or every showPetById entry with the data typed.
  queryClient.setQueryData(showPetByIdQueryKey({ path: { petId } }, scope), (old) => old && { ...old, name });
  setShowPetByIdQueriesData(queryClient, (old) => old && { ...old, name }, scope);
}

export function signOut(): void {
  queryClient.removeQueries(queryScopeFilter(scope));
}

void useCreatePet;
```

- Keys are `[operationId, data]`, or `[{ scope }, operationId, data]` for a client with `queryScope`; build them with `{function}QueryKey(data, scope)`, never by hand.
- Paginated lists: write the pagination on the operation (`x-tsurara-pagination: { param: query.cursor, next: /nextCursor }`) or in `typescript.infiniteQueries`; the read then has `{function}InfiniteQueryOptions`, for `useInfiniteQuery`.
- The options throw `ApiError` (they `unwrap`); `error.result` is the Result, so branch with `isHttpError(error.result, status)` and `error.kind`.

Tests use the generated handlers; each takes a documented response, or a function of the request that returns one:

```ts
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node';
import { handlers } from './mocks/index.js';
import { showPetByIdHandler } from './mocks/operations/showPetById.js';
import { mockPet } from './mocks/schemas/Pet.js';

const server = setupServer(...handlers);
server.listen({ onUnhandledFrame: 'error' }); // MSW 3; `onUnhandledRequest` in MSW 2
server.use(showPetByIdHandler(({ params }) => ({ status: 200, body: mockPet({ id: Number(params.petId) }) })));
```

<!-- skills/tsurara/references/typescript.md -->

# TypeScript

Each operation is a function `operationId(client, options)` in `operations/`, with types `{Op}Data` (its input), `{Op}Result` (every outcome) and the schema types in `schemas/`. Create one client per base URL and pass it explicitly.

```ts
import { createClient, unwrap } from '@tsurara/client';
import { showPetById } from './operations/showPetById.js';
import type { Pet } from './schemas/Pet.js';

const api = createClient({ baseUrl: 'https://petstore.example.com/v1' });

// Results never throw: check `ok`, then `kind`.
export async function petName(petId: string): Promise<string | undefined> {
  const result = await showPetById(api, { path: { petId } });
  if (result.ok) {
    return result.data.name;
  }
  if (result.kind === 'http' && result.documented) {
    console.error(result.status, result.error.message); // the documented error body
  } else {
    console.error(result.kind); // network, timeout, aborted, parse, ...
  }
  return undefined;
}

// Where an exception is right (inside a TanStack Query queryFn, a script): `unwrap` returns the data
// or throws `ApiError` with the Result.
export async function loadPet(petId: string): Promise<Pet> {
  return unwrap(await showPetById(api, { path: { petId } }));
}
```

- Imports end in the configured extension (`.js` by default, `.ts` with `typescript.importExtension: ts`).
- `{ path, query, headers, cookies, body }` follow the definition; optional parameters can be left out.
- Request bodies of several media types take `contentType` next to `body`.
- `createClient` options: `headers`, `auth` (per security scheme), `timeout`, `middleware`, `onResult`, `validate` (with the generated Zod schemas, `typescript.validators: zod`), `queryScope` (TanStack Query keys).
- With TanStack Query or MSW, read [tanstack-query.md](tanstack-query.md): use the generated options and handlers, not a hand-written `queryFn`, key or handler.
